description: Synthetic migration cases with expectations based on SQL semantics, not captured engine output. A missing finding for one rule is not a database safety guarantee.

cases.reason: Schema-qualified built-in random remains volatile; qualification must not hide the rewrite risk.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ADD COLUMN sample float8 DEFAULT pg_catalog.random();

cases.reason: PostgreSQL 11 can use a fast default for stable CURRENT_TIMESTAMP; the table still needs a DDL lock.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ADD COLUMN recorded_at timestamptz DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;

cases.reason: Before PostgreSQL 11 even a literal default uses the older rewrite behavior.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ADD COLUMN retries int DEFAULT 0;

cases.reason: A user-defined function name does not reveal volatility or prove a physical rewrite.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ADD COLUMN label text DEFAULT app.make_label();

cases.reason: An ordinary expression index still takes the write-blocking CREATE INDEX table lock.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; CREATE INDEX readings_label_lower ON readings ((lower(label))) WHERE label IS NOT NULL;

cases.reason: CONCURRENTLY removes this rule's ordinary-index finding, without proving runner transaction settings or index eligibility.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY readings_label_lower ON readings ((lower(label))) WHERE label IS NOT NULL;

cases.reason: A table populated in the migration must not retain the empty-new-table exemption.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; CREATE TABLE readings (id int); INSERT INTO readings VALUES(1),(2); CREATE INDEX readings_id ON readings(id);

cases.reason: A directly validated composite foreign key needs the validation-risk finding even with action and deferrability clauses.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE details ADD CONSTRAINT details_parent FOREIGN KEY(tenant_id,parent_id) REFERENCES parents(tenant_id,id) ON DELETE CASCADE DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED;

cases.reason: NOT VALID deliberately postpones the existing-row check; it does not prove the child has an index.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE details ADD CONSTRAINT details_parent FOREIGN KEY(tenant_id,parent_id) REFERENCES parents(tenant_id,id) ON DELETE CASCADE DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED NOT VALID;

cases.reason: A target type alone cannot establish the source type or rewrite requirement.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ALTER COLUMN label TYPE text;

cases.reason: Known varchar widening avoids a heap rewrite on the target version but retains ACCESS EXCLUSIVE acquisition.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ALTER COLUMN label TYPE varchar(40);

cases.reason: An empty table created in the same file has no existing rows requiring production rewrite analysis.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; CREATE TABLE readings(label int); ALTER TABLE readings ALTER COLUMN label TYPE bigint;

cases.reason: DEFERRABLE changes enforcement timing, not the direct index-build lock risk.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ADD CONSTRAINT readings_label_unique UNIQUE(label) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED;

cases.reason: Attaching an existing concurrent unique index must not be reported as a direct unique-index build.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY readings_label_unique ON readings(label); ALTER TABLE readings ADD CONSTRAINT readings_label_unique UNIQUE USING INDEX readings_label_unique;

cases.reason: IF EXISTS does not remove compatibility risk if the column does exist; CASCADE needs separate review.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS legacy_label CASCADE;

cases.reason: DROP COLUMN inside a quoted additive column name must not be mistaken for a destructive SQL action.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ADD COLUMN "drop column" text;

cases.reason: VACUUM FULL is an exclusive maintenance rewrite even without an explicit BEGIN.
cases.sql: VACUUM (FULL, ANALYZE) readings;

cases.reason: A fillfactor change must not trigger an autovacuum-specific recommendation.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings SET (fillfactor=85);

cases.reason: Zero means no lock timeout and cannot protect subsequent DDL waits.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout=0; ALTER TABLE readings ADD COLUMN note text;

cases.reason: A positive millisecond setting before DDL is effective for this rule.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='250ms'; ALTER TABLE readings ADD COLUMN note text;

cases.reason: An unvalidated CHECK does not prove the absence of pre-existing NULL rows.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ADD CONSTRAINT label_present CHECK(label IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; ALTER TABLE readings ALTER COLUMN label SET NOT NULL;

cases.reason: PostgreSQL 12 can use a validated CHECK to skip SET NOT NULL's existing-row scan.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ADD CONSTRAINT label_present CHECK(label IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; ALTER TABLE readings VALIDATE CONSTRAINT label_present; ALTER TABLE readings ALTER COLUMN label SET NOT NULL;

cases.reason: The validated-CHECK scan optimization starts in PostgreSQL 12; the same sequence on PostgreSQL 11 still needs the risk finding.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ADD CONSTRAINT label_present CHECK(label IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; ALTER TABLE readings VALIDATE CONSTRAINT label_present; ALTER TABLE readings ALTER COLUMN label SET NOT NULL;

cases.reason: An imported snapshot's newer version cannot enable optimizations absent in the explicitly selected PostgreSQL 11 target.
cases.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE readings(label text CONSTRAINT label_present CHECK(label IS NOT NULL));
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ALTER COLUMN label SET NOT NULL;

cases.reason: The selected PostgreSQL 17 target supports the scan optimization even when the supplied validated CHECK was captured using a PostgreSQL 11 snapshot.
cases.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE readings(label text CONSTRAINT label_present CHECK(label IS NOT NULL));
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; ALTER TABLE readings ALTER COLUMN label SET NOT NULL;

cases.reason: ROLLBACK undoes the added and validated CHECK, so it cannot prove that a later SET NOT NULL avoids scanning existing rows.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; BEGIN; ALTER TABLE readings ADD CONSTRAINT label_present CHECK(label IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; ALTER TABLE readings VALIDATE CONSTRAINT label_present; ROLLBACK; ALTER TABLE readings ALTER COLUMN label SET NOT NULL;

cases.reason: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY is prohibited in an explicit transaction just like its CREATE counterpart.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; BEGIN; DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY readings_label_unique; COMMIT;

cases.reason: A completed preceding transaction does not make a following standalone concurrent drop transactional.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; BEGIN; SELECT 1; COMMIT; DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY readings_label_unique;

cases.reason: An INCLUDE column alone is not an index search key for the foreign-key lookup.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY details_payload ON details(payload) INCLUDE(parent_id); ALTER TABLE details ADD CONSTRAINT details_parent FOREIGN KEY(parent_id) REFERENCES parents(id) NOT VALID;

cases.reason: A btree whose leading keys cover the composite foreign key supports the equality lookup; trailing keys do not invalidate it.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY details_parent_lookup ON details(tenant_id,parent_id,payload); ALTER TABLE details ADD CONSTRAINT details_parent FOREIGN KEY(tenant_id,parent_id) REFERENCES parents(tenant_id,id) NOT VALID;

cases.reason: The equality lookup constrains both leading btree keys even when their order differs from the foreign-key declaration.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY details_parent_lookup ON details(parent_id,tenant_id,payload); ALTER TABLE details ADD CONSTRAINT details_parent FOREIGN KEY(tenant_id,parent_id) REFERENCES parents(tenant_id,id) NOT VALID;

cases.reason: Every explicitly truncated existing relation has the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE/data-removal risk.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; TRUNCATE readings, details CONTINUE IDENTITY RESTRICT;

cases.reason: Concurrent refresh avoids the ordinary REFRESH finding; eligibility still requires a populated view and suitable unique index in the actual database.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY readings_summary;

cases.reason: A DO block's string contents must not be mistaken for fully analyzed SQL or receive an all-clear result.
cases.sql: DO $body$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'CREATE INDEX readings_id ON readings(id)'; END $body$;

cases.reason: Ignoring an enabled rule changes coverage even if it removes the only visible finding.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; CREATE INDEX readings_id ON readings(id);

cases.reason: A statement-level suppression must remain visible as incomplete rule coverage, not a clean pass.
cases.sql: SET lock_timeout='3s'; /* lockguard-ignore: LG-002 */ CREATE INDEX readings_id ON readings(id);
